conventions.convention: Admissible curves on [a,b], a<b, are restrictions of C² maps on an open interval containing [a,b]; variations are C² and vanish at both endpoints. The action chart requires a nonempty open configuration domain.
L=K−U contains only the potential part of F=−∇U+d. Pure stationarity gives the full force-model equation only on the branch d≡0.
The Euler–Lagrange expression is E_L=L_x−dL_v/dt, hence E_L=−(Mx''+∇U). The Lagrange operator Λ uses the opposite sign.

A generalized-coordinate map X:Ω→Q is C³ with injective derivative. Full-dimensional maps give local coordinates; global charts additionally require injectivity. Constraint parametrizations have r=3N−k, cover C∩Q, and need not be one-to-one.
G_ij has dimension mass·length²/(γ_iγ_j), and generalized force component i has dimension energy/γ_i. L has energy dimension and S has action dimension.
The gauge function is C³ on the full time-configuration domain and has action dimension. Potential shifts c(t) are C²; scaling preserves stationary curves only for nonzero dimensionless factors.

The nonholonomic example uses dimensionless s=t/T₀ and coordinates r/L₀. Primes there denote derivatives with respect to s, and vakonomic motion means stationarity of the specified augmented functional, not an unspecified constrained minimization problem.

load_bearing.statement: For the adopted force model with fixed positive masses and potential presentation F=−∇U+d, U∈C²(I₀×Q), define K(v)=½v·Mv and L(t,x,v)=K(v)−U(t,x). On a nonempty open Q and [a,b]⊂I₀ with a<b, instantiate the mathematical action chart, its C² admissible curves, fixed-endpoint variations and stationarity.

For the stated mechanical presentation, a C² admissible curve x:[a,b]→Q and a fixed-endpoint variation η, the first variation exists and equals ∫[−∇U(t,x(t))·η(t)+Mx'(t)·η'(t)]dt; E_L(x)(t)=−(Mx''(t)+∇U(t,x(t))) for every t∈[a,b].

Under the stated force-model and C² potential-presentation hypotheses, for a C² admissible curve x:[a,b]→Q, stationarity for S, E_L(x)=0 on [a,b], and Mx''=−∇U(t,x) on [a,b] are equivalent. Residual forces do not appear, and no existence is asserted.

For a C³ immersion X:Ω→Q, define the substituted Lagrangian L̃(t,q,v)=L(t,X(q),DX(q)v), G=DXᵀMDX, and generalized force Q_f(t,q,v)=DX(q)ᵀf(t,X(q),DX(q)v). The declared Lagrange equations are Λ(L̃)(q)=Q_d(t,q,q'). Constraint parametrizations have the stated full-coverage and ambient-domain hypotheses.

For nonempty open Ω⊂Rⁿ and Q⊂Rᵐ, a C³ map X:Ω→Q, and C² L:J×Q×Rᵐ→R on an open interval J, L̃(t,q,v)=L(t,X(q),DX(q)v) is C². Along every C² curve q:J'→Ω on an interval J'⊂J with nonempty interior, E_L̃(q)=DX(q)ᵀE_L(X∘q). No rank assumption is required.

For the adopted force model, potential presentation, regular scleronomic holonomic datum, ideal-reaction law and stated C³ full-coverage immersed parametrization, a C² coordinate curve solves Λ(L̃)=Q_d exactly when its induced configuration curve is an ideal constrained motion. The reaction and continuous multiplier are unique, and virtual displacements equal im DX. No solution existence or uniqueness of coordinate curves is asserted.

On the global potential branch d≡0, every motion restricts to a stationary curve on each closed [a,b] inside its interval. Conversely, every C² stationary admissible curve on [a,b]⊂I₀ is the restriction of the unique maximal motion through (a,x(a),x'(a)), whose maximal interval contains [a,b].

For the stated C³ time-dependent map X with invertible X_q and substituted domain, E_L̃(q)=X_qᵀE_L(x) along the given C² curve, so the substituted equation is equivalent to the Cartesian potential-part equation. Stationarity equivalence additionally assumes a common open configuration set W with [a,b]×W×R³ᴺ contained in the substituted domain.

concerns.concern: The last remark says: “The plane-polar case is the restriction z≡const, in which the third equation is dropped.” The declared model permits arbitrary C² U(t,x,y,z), so this restriction need not satisfy the model equation. For U=mgz, every motion has z''=−g; dropping the third equation incorrectly admits constant-z curves. State a separate ideal planar constraint or the necessary condition ∂zU=0 along the restricted curve.

Clause (e) says the equations with residual generalized force are the coordinate form of the model equation “as the covariance theorem of this page records.” pthm-cm07-coordinate-covariance-of-the-equations explicitly excludes residual forces and proves only the potential-part equation. The residual-force extension follows immediately from the transport identity and E_L=−d along a motion, but that extension is not the cited theorem's stated conclusion.

The normalization introduces L₀, T₀ and m₀ by their dimensions, then divides by L₀ and T₀ and calls m₀L₀²/T₀ a “positive multiple.” Explicit positivity hypotheses for these scales are missing. Dimensions alone do not ensure nonzero denominators or the asserted positive factor.

alerts.finding: Clause (a) allows G of class C², then says “by [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] the set Σ_t is an embedded submanifold.” The opened theorem assumes a smooth map, and def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart requires smooth slice charts. Rank-regular C² data need not have a smooth embedded zero set: in numerical coordinates, G(t,x,y,z)=y−|x|³ has rank-one spatial derivative everywhere, but its zero set is a C² graph that is not C³ at x=0. The finite-regularity conclusion requires different terminology and a matching supplier, or stronger hypotheses.

Clause (f) assumes U:Q→R is C² and ∇U≠0 on the nonempty level, then concludes “U⁻¹(c) is an embedded submanifold of Q” by the smooth regular-level theorem. The opened theorem requires smoothness, and the linked embedded-submanifold definition is smooth. U(x,y,z)=y−|x|³ has a nowhere-zero gradient and a nonempty zero level, but that level is not a smooth embedded submanifold. The asserted regularity exceeds the stated hypotheses.

seams_checked.note: The oscillator saddle and boundary-value nonuniqueness are cited qualitatively with their interval-dependent scope; no minimization or endpoint-existence conclusion is added.

Reduction retains the regular scleronomic datum and adopted ideal-reaction condition. The supplier's separate smoothness defect is routed in alerts; the reduction's kernel/rank argument does not require that overstrong conclusion.
Newton equivalence uses the standing force regularity, unique maximal motion and compact continuation criterion without claiming global existence.
Positive masses, the fixed inertial frame, open ambient configuration domain, mass operator and unit conventions are preserved.
The C² potential presentation, residual split and componentwise potential-normalization freedom are used faithfully; exactness is not inferred from closedness.
The action chart, fixed-endpoint stationarity, covariance, gauge and multiplier statements retain their regularity and domain hypotheses.
The declared free, oscillator, uniform-field and potential models satisfy the standing force assumptions; calculations are model values.
The examples declare their potential representatives and use zero residual force where full stationary-action equivalence is claimed.
Mass, length, time, angle and multiplier dimensions agree with the framework conventions; the normalization-scale omission is recorded separately.
The explicit d'Alembert solution and vakonomic contradiction match the mathematical counterexample, including nonstationarity on every nondegenerate interval.
The pendulum uses a smooth rank-two constraint and an adopted ideal reaction; the reaction and differently dimensioned multiplier components are computed consistently.
Noether consumers preserve L=K−U, the d≡0 condition for pure stationarity, residual-force rates and the C³ moving-map transport hypotheses.
Worked potentials and the rotating chart use the mechanical Lagrangian and coordinate covariance with zero residual forces.
The quadratic-model definition uses the kinetic metric at equilibrium and the energy-per-coordinate generalized-force dimensions without treating linearization as exact nonlinear dynamics.
Momentum, kinetic metric, residual-force Hamilton equations, closed-interval stationarity and ideal constraint elimination retain the supplier hypotheses.
Gauge and moving-coordinate examples use the stated transport laws. The pendulum restricts the ambient datum to each angular chart before applying the full-coverage reduction theorem.
The generalized-coordinate momentum construction retains C³ immersions and G=DXᵀMDX; the model-equation statement separates zero-residual and forced branches.
The point-transformation example requires a full-dimensional invertible DX, and mechanical examples explicitly declare their potentials and residual-force branch.
The mechanical presentation and generalized-coordinate dictionary are preserved; the characteristic theorem conditions its identification with model motions on d≡0.
The free and harmonic counterexamples use the declared zero-residual mechanical branch and do not strengthen stationary-action equivalence.
The page requirement is background context: its item inventory has no direct cm07 supplier use, and its prose does not extend the finite-particle action theorem to continuum fields.
